Participant.description: Someone the network deals with. `type` says which kind, and decides which of the remaining fields apply: a node speaks Beckn and is addressed by its participantId; an upstream is an ordinary API our adapter calls. No credential of ours appears here — how to authenticate to an upstream is the binding's plugin's, read from the adapter's own environment.

baseUrl.description: The base something is appended to: a Beckn action for a node, a binding's path for an upstream. https for a node. An upstream may be plaintext: with no auth field the registry cannot tell whether a call to it carries a credential, so it cannot condition the transport rule on one — that guard now sits with the binding's plugin, which holds the credential.

role.description: What this node does on the network. BAP asks. BPP answers. NETWORK exposes publish and discover, answering discover from published catalogs.

allOf.description: A node speaks Beckn: it needs a role and a key, and its id is its wire identity so it must be a hostname.
An upstream does not speak Beckn: it has no role on the network and no keys we verify. It is one host and a base path, nothing more.

PublicKey.description: A node's public key, held as material: it is public, so there is nothing to protect. It is the only key material in these three schemas, and there is no secret in them at all.

keyId.description: Second field of the Authorization keyId, so a sender can say which key it signed with.

use.description: sign verifies signatures; encrypt is for encrypted payloads. A node holds one key, so it holds one or the other.

alg.description: Fixed by use. Both curves are 32-byte keys.

key.description: base64 of the 32 raw bytes: 44 chars, one trailing '='. A truncated or wrong-curve key fails at write time.

validUntil.description: Absent means open-ended. There is one key, so it has no successor to overlap with: a validUntil in the past leaves the node unable to sign, and rotation is a full replace of this object.

status.description: revoked withdraws the key early. Effective only once the reader refreshes.

ParticipantId.description: Stable id, and the only id. For a node this is its network identity (context.bapId / context.bppId); for an upstream it is the Beckn offer.provider.id.

ParticipantType.description: node speaks Beckn. upstream is an API we call over ordinary HTTP and does not.
